title: Real-time stream chunk insights and redaction workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a pragmatic, low-latency observability surface for LLM streaming that exposes per-chunk metrics, correlated OpenTelemetry traces, and a deterministic redaction workflow so logs/metrics do not leak PII or sensitive tool output. This work ties together runtime instrumentation, the tracing pipeline, and log/metrics processors to support: debugging slow chunk emits, quantifying incremental token cost, and auditing streamed tool calls while guaranteeing redaction before any persisted logs or dashboards.

Goals:
- Emit standardized per-chunk metrics for every streaming response: chunk_index, chunk_token_delta, chunk_latency_ms, chunk_size_bytes, encoder_queue_time_ms, kv_cache_hit (bool), model_variant.
- Produce trace spans that correlate request -> stream -> chunk (span names: request.handle, stream.open, stream.chunk.emit) with stable identifiers (request_id, stream_id, chunk_id) and minimal high-cardinality tags.
- Implement a redaction pipeline that runs at the telemetry ingress layer to remove PII and suppress sensitive tool outputs before metrics/logs/traces are written to long-term storage.
- Backwards-compatible SDK behavior: older SDKs that only surface full-response events should still produce metrics with fallback chunk_index=0 and a note in tags.

Non-goals:
- Full schema of all model internals. We will not attempt to capture token-level embeddings or raw token text in durable logs.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
1) Metrics vs traces: metrics will carry numeric summaries per chunk (latency and token delta); traces will carry the causal timeline. This keeps time-series costs lower while enabling deep inspection via sampled traces.
2) Redaction location: perform redaction at the telemetry collector (Edge/ingest) rather than in the runtime to maintain a single policy surface and avoid repeating logic in all runtimes. Runtime will tag sensitive segments and add minimal metadata to aid redaction.
3) Sampling: to control trace volume, we will use adaptive sampling keyed by error rate and latency SLO violations. Chunks with latency > p95 or which trigger tool calls are high-priority for sampling.

Telemetry schemas (expected fields - metric labels are strings):
- metric name: stream.chunk.latency_ms, type: histogram, labels: request_id, stream_id, model, model_variant, route, chunk_index
- metric name: stream.chunk.tokens, type: counter, labels: request_id, stream_id, model, chunk_index
- trace span attributes (OTel semantic): request_id, stream_id, chunk_id, chunk_index, chunk_token_delta, model_variant, kv_cache_hit (true/false), route

Redaction rules (high level):
- Tagging: runtime emits a tag sensitive=true for segments that include tool outputs or content flagged by the safety filter. Tagging must be conservative (prefer false negatives over false positives) and not include raw text.
- Ingest redactor behavior: for any telemetry marked sensitive=true, strip any textual attributes and replace with redaction.reason values such as "TOOL_OUTPUT" or "PII_DETECTED". Numeric metrics remain unchanged.
- Deterministic ID hashing: where identifiers must be preserved for correlation (e.g., chunk_id), the collector will hash IDs with a stable salt per-customer. The salt is managed by the control plane for hosted tenants and by the customer in Private deployments.
- Audit mode: enterprise customers can opt-in to an encrypted archival path where raw content is stored in customer-controlled storage with separate access controls; this path is out of band from standard dashboards.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime emits the defined per-chunk metrics and OTel spans for 95% of streaming sessions in the staging env.
- Ingest redactor tests demonstrate PII samples are removed and replaced with allowed redaction reasons (automated test coverage).
- Dashboards: new Stream Insights dashboard shows chunk-level latency distribution, chunk token histogram, and top routes by chunk emit failures.
- Backcompat: SDK integration tests show older SDK clients map to metrics with chunk_index=0 and no errors.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Instrument runtime to emit per-chunk counter/latency metrics and attach stable IDs (ENG).
- Week 2: Add OTel span instrumentation and wire into temporary debug collector (ENG).
- Week 3: Implement ingest-side redactor & deterministic hashing; provide local test harness for PII samples (Platform).
- Week 4: Dashboards and alerting; define adaptive sampling policy for traces (Observability).
- Week 5: Canary rollout to 10% of traffic with monitoring and rollback plan (SRE + Product).

Open questions / risks:
- How to keep labels low-cardinality while still enabling useful group-bys? Proposal: model_variant and route are the primary dimensions; avoid tagging by customer_id in metrics.
- Cost impact of increased metrics cardinality and trace volume—need an estimate from billing team before wide rollout.
- Redaction false negatives: safety filter tuning required to avoid leaking PII.

Files & artifacts to produce:
- Runtime PR with instrumentation: github.com/redwood/rt-infer/pull/XXXX
- Ingest redactor implementation: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/YYYY
- Dashboard JSON and Grafana/Looker queries: /dashboards/stream-insights.json
- Design doc: confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFER/Stream+Chunk+Observability

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on the redaction boundary and sampling policy. If we decide to do redaction inside the runtime instead of the collector, runtime complexity increases significantly and will slow feature rollout.
